data.one_liner: Schema validation library with bidirectional codecs and JSON Schema support.
data.what_it_does: Ack provides schema validation and bidirectional codecs for Dart and Flutter. It allows developers to define validation rules using a fluent API, validate external payloads against schemas, import and export JSON Schemas, and generate immutable models.
use_when: You need to validate incoming API payloads and user inputs against structured rules.
You want bidirectional codecs that handle both parsing and serialization in a single definition.
You need to import or export JSON Schema definitions in your Dart/Flutter applications.
avoid_when: You are already heavily invested in built_value or json_serializable for your serialization needs and do not want to migrate.
You only need simple state management or dependency injection.
strengths: Fluent, easy-to-read API for defining complex data validation logic.
Built-in JSON Schema import and export support.
Reduces boilerplate for validation and JSON conversion.
weaknesses: Requires migrating away from other annotation systems if you adopt its built-in code generation via `@Schemable()`.
Full A2UI coverage is not supported.
data.setup_notes: Add ack to pubspec.yaml and import 'package:ack/ack.dart'.

alternatives.name: json_serializable
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer standard annotation-based JSON serialization without custom schema validation logic.

alternatives.name: freezed
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your primary goal is generating immutable union types and data classes with built-in copyWith and equality.
